content.text: Anrufen (meaning 'to call') is an elegant Austrian trick-taking game belonging to the Marriage family. It is distinguished by its 'Call-a-Card' partner selection and a simplified scoring system where only 'Gwisse' (Aces, Tens, and the Last Trick) carry numerical value. It combines the secret partnerships of bridge with the point-collecting mechanics of MariÃ¡Å¡.
A descendant of the 18th-century French game 'Mariage', which spread across the Austro-Hungarian Empire. The Austrian version settled into a 24-card format common in the Salzburg and Alpine regions.
24 cards. Using French suits (A-10-K-Q-J-9) or German suits (A-10-K-O-U-9).
Standard 32-card deck (remove 7s and 8s), score sheet or tokens.
Each player is dealt 6 cards in batches of 3-3. Bidding rotates clockwise starting from the dealer's left.

items.text: Graden Style: No 'Simple' bid allowed. If all pass, the hand is played as 'Schurln' (lowest score loses).
3-Player Anrufen: 7 cards each and a 3-card talon. High bidder plays alone against two.
